issues.problem: The negative role is described as a 'hypothetical teammate' without a concrete user_id, channel binding beyond C_INFRA, or membership record, making it under-specified relative to the other roles (which cite exact IDs/messages).
issues.repair: Give this negative role a concrete user_id and confirm/plan its channel_members row, or drop it since existing negatives already cover membership-without-authorship contrast is not truly needed.

rationale: The route USER→MESSAGE→CONVERSATION→WORKSPACE is faithfully translated: selection is anchored on message authorship (not mere channel membership), and the two 'Robert' matches (Robert Walsh in #engineering, Robert Chen in #core-infra) each independently satisfy 'named Robert + numeric-problem message + bounded technical channel corpus,' correctly justifying the underspecified resolution mode per the binding_note. The negatives (silent-member Robert with no message, Kenji with numeric content but wrong name/channel, off-topic Robert Walsh message) exercise real distinguishing dimensions (authorship vs membership, name, channel scope, content) without leaking the answer. Referenced channels/messages for Robert Chen and the off-topic Robert Walsh message already exist in the base seed; the still-missing Robert Walsh qualifying message is an acceptable planned addition at this design-review stage. The two obligations use only legitimate table.column names, and the access_plan/task_spec correctly rely on documented APIs (conversations.history, users.info, conversations.open, chat.postMessage) without invoking unavailable capabilities (no membership-join-time or edit-history lookups). The single minor gap is the underspecified/thin description of the 'robert_silent_member' negative role, which does not affect the core validity of the underspecified design.
